message.content:
**Typical number of mitochondria per cell**

| Cell type | Typical range of mitochondria per cell |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| **General somatic cells** (e.g., fibroblasts, epithelial cells) | ~100–500 |
| **Neurons** (especially axons) | ~200–1 000 |
| **Muscle cells** (skeletal, cardiac) | ~1 000–10 000 |
| **Red blood cells** (mature erythrocytes) | 0 (they lose mitochondria during maturation) |

> **Key points**
> - The exact number varies widely depending on the cell’s metabolic demand and differentiation state.
> - Cells with high energy requirements (cardiomyocytes, skeletal muscle fibers, neurons) contain thousands of mitochondria to meet ATP demands.
> - Some specialized cells (e.g., mature red blood cells) lack mitochondria entirely.

If you’d like more detailed information about mitochondrial functions or how their numbers change during development, let me know!
